title: Horizon — Model picklist & catalog selection walkthrough
next_steps: Send security and SOC2 + KMS integration docs
Share benchmark spreadsheet with latency/cost scenarios
Schedule a 1-hour POC scoping call next week (SE + Platform)
Provide sample API keys for a 48-hour smoke test in the hosted sandbox
action_items: Maya Patel: Email SOC2 and KMS doc + short how-to for VPC peering (due 2025-10-02)
Liam Chen: Export example benchmark queries from Redwood Optimize and add to shared sheet (due 2025-10-03)
Priya Iyer: Share current traffic patterns + SLOs for inference (due 2025-10-01)
Carlos Reyes: Confirm timeline for pilot and procurement constraints (due 2025-10-06)
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Time: 15:00 - 15:58 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood SE); Carlos Reyes (Horizon CTO), Janelle Moore (ML Eng), Priya Iyer (Platform), Evan Liu (SRE)
summary: Redwood ran a focused walkthrough of the model catalog picklist, benchmark interpretations from Redwood Optimize, and compatibility considerations for Horizon's privacy-sensitive health workloads. Horizon expressed interest in hosted sandbox for quick validation but flagged VPC/on-prem and KMS requirements for production. SE asked for traffic patterns and SLOs; next step is a POC scoping call and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya here from Redwood, I think we have about 55, 58 minutes on the calendar, is that right?
[00:06] Carlos Reyes: Yep that works for us, thanks Maya.
[00:09] Maya Patel: Cool. Quick introductions then I can hand over to Liam for the catalog picklist flow, and we'll cover how Optimize surfaces bench tradeoffs.
[00:17] Janelle Moore: Hi, Janelle, ML Eng. We mostly run inference on a mix of managed instances but for PHI-sensitive flows we push to our VPC or on-prem clusters.
[00:26] Priya Iyer: Priya, platform - I own the infra side and peering.
[00:29] Liam Chen: Liam, SE at Redwood — I'll show the catalog then run a few benchmark scenarios.
[00:33] Noah Rivera: Noah from solutions if we need to dive into routing details.
[00:36] Evan Liu: Evan, SRE. We'll be interested in autoscaling behavior.
[00:40] Maya Patel: Great. Quick agenda: 1) how Horizon can pick open models from the catalog for different tasks, 2) how Optimize interprets bench signal for latency vs cost, 3) compatibility matrix mapping to kernel/quantization, and 4) next steps for a pilot.
[00:55] Liam Chen: Alright I'm sharing my screen - start with the catalog home. You can see we surface model metadata first - architecture, tokenization quirks, recommended sequence lengths. For picklisting we usually recommend starting with three candidates per intent: a high-accuracy baseline, a mid-cost quantized variant, and a fastest low-cost variant.
[01:18] Janelle Moore: When you say quantized variant, do you mean you host a separately quantized copy or is that a runtime switch?
[01:22] Liam Chen: Good call out. Right now it's a distinct model artifact — we keep both the FP16 and the int8 builds in the catalog. Runtime will pick the appropriate variant based on routing policy. So you can pin a model by artifact ID if you want consistency.
[01:37] Carlos Reyes: For our compliance team, we need to know what happens to KV cache material — is that retained across requests in hosted mode?
[01:44] Noah Rivera: In hosted we maintain ephemeral KV caches - they live only for the session unless you enable explicit prefix caching for reuse. Those caches are encrypted at rest, but for strict PHI rules we usually recommend private deployment with customer-managed KMS.
[01:58] Priya Iyer: So private deployment it is then for production - what's the lift?
[02:03] Liam Chen: For a standard VPC private deployment we do control plane integration into your VPC peering, and customer KMS for key management. The console will show RBAC + per-token cost. We have a guide — Maya can send the doc.
[02:14] Maya Patel: I'll share the SOC2 and KMS integration notes after the call, plus a short checklist.
[02:20] Evan Liu: Sounds good. Curious on benchmarks — you said Optimize can recommend which model/quant version to pick depending on throughput. Can you demo?
[02:27] Liam Chen: Yep. Switching to the Optimize view — here we ingest traces and synthetic bench runs. For this demo I preloaded three traces with different seq lengths: short (customer-facing prompts ~40 tokens), medium (summaries ~150 tokens), long (reports ~600 tokens).
[02:43] [02:45] Liam Chen: Here is a scatter - x axis is median latency, y axis is cost per 1k tokens — you can pick a latency SLO and it filters models. For example if you set 200ms SLO for 95th, it eliminates the bigger FP16 models but recommends an int8 variant or a different architecture that has better kernel support on our target GPUs.
[03:04] Janelle Moore: The plots look useful. How accurate are these estimates? We run a lot of short-burst traffic.
[03:09] Liam Chen: Estimates are from microbench harnesses + simulated batching based on your trace. For short-burst traffic the batching variance is lower, so we surface percentile bands. I'd call them directional but within 10-15% of real runs; we encourage a pilot bench run to confirm.
[03:25] Carlos Reyes: Does Redwood support automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes? We can't have production failures.
[03:29] Noah Rivera: Yes — routing policies can be set to degrade gracefully: prefer model A, fallback to model B if queue depth exceeds threshold or if observed latency breaches SLO. That switch is live and stateless — requests will route to the fallback instance.
[03:43] Priya Iyer: Can we do weighted traffic splits for canaries?
[03:46] Liam Chen: Absolutely — the rollout UI supports canary percentages, A/B, and time-based ramps, plus automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts.
[03:55] Evan Liu: On the kernel/compatibility matrix - do you have a simple way to flag models that require special kernels or fused attention?
[04:01] Liam Chen: Yes the catalog has a compatibility table per artifact: supported kernels, recommended sequence length, memory profile, and our confidence score for quantized execution. It also tags models that need custom kernels or that are currently incompatible with our fastest path.
[04:16] [04:18] Liam Chen: I'll pull up an example: see Model X-LLM - it has good accuracy on clinical prompts but poor int8 support; Optimize marks that quantization causes hallucination risk on instruction-tuning. We show the delta across prompts in the bench sheet.
[04:33] Janelle Moore: Hallucination delta — is that automated evals on your side?
[04:36] Liam Chen: It's a mix — we run a set of canonical prompt evals, plus your own prompt set if you share. The Optimize alert ties quality regressions to specific prompt groups so you can see where quantization or a kernel change impacts outputs.
[04:50] Carlos Reyes: That seems useful — in our case the clinical hallucination risk is a blocker, so we'd want to ensure the mid-cost candidate still passes those evals.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Exactly. Our recommended picklist process is: 1) choose 3 candidates, 2) vet them with your prompt set in Optimize, 3) run an automated bench in your infra (or our hosted sandbox) and 4) choose a rollout strategy with fallback.
[05:13] Evan Liu: For the hosted sandbox, what data residency guarantees exist?
[05:18] Noah Rivera: Hosted sandbox is region-isolated but not suitable for PHI by default; it's intended for smoke tests. For PHI you should use Private with your KMS and VPC.
[05:27] Priya Iyer: Procurement question — what’s the pricing delta between hosted and dedicated? Ballpark numbers?
[05:31] Maya Patel: Ballpark — hosted is usage-based; dedicated/reserved gives you predictability and lower per-token costs at commit. We'll send a pricing sheet but final numbers depend on expected token volumes and reserved commitment.
[05:43] Janelle Moore: Can we get a sample benchmark that matches our short-burst profile?
[05:46] Liam Chen: Yes, share your trace and we'll run it through Optimize. We can also provide a reproducible bench run you can run in your VPC.
[05:54] [06:00] -- Timestamps advance as Liam walks through the picklist UI and a shared benchmark sheet --
[06:12] Liam Chen: Here is the shared bench sheet link: (internal) https://redwood.app/sheets/bench/horizon-demo — includes the three seq groups and the per-model cost/latency.
[06:26] Janelle Moore: Noted — when you say "per-token cost" does that include tokenization mismatch costs? We use a different tokenizer in our preprocessor sometimes.
[06:33] Liam Chen: The catalog shows the tokenizer type and a tokenization multiplier if you use a non-standard preprocessor. That multiplier is empirical — we recommend running a short trace to confirm.
[06:42] Carlos Reyes: On the subject of SSO and audit logs — we need full audit trails for inference calls and per-user role control.
[06:50] Maya Patel: Redwood Console supports SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC roles, and audit logs with byte-level anonymization options. For Private we can push audit logs to your logging buckets.
[06:59] Evan Liu: And retention?
[07:01] Noah Rivera: Retention is configurable; for PHI we recommend short retention windows plus export-to-GCS/S3 for long-term storage under your control.
[07:09] [07:12] Janelle Moore: Back to the matrix — you mentioned confidence scores for quantized runs. What's the typical false-positive rate on those confidence signals?
[07:18] Liam Chen: Good question; the confidence score is conservative — it errs on the side of flagging potential regressions. For our internal evals the FP rate is lower than 10% but it depends on dataset skew. We always recommend running your own validation set.
[07:33] Carlos Reyes: Let's scope a POC. We want: hosted sandbox smoke test for two intents, and a private pilot for one service endpoint with VPC peering, KMS integration, and load testing against our short-burst trace. What's the timeline you see?
[07:49] Maya Patel: Realistically, sandbox smoke test in 48 hours, bench analysis in 3 business days after you share traces, and private pilot for infra setup in 2-3 weeks depending on procurement.
[07:59] Priya Iyer: Procurement could take longer but we can start work in parallel.
[08:03] [08:05] Liam Chen: For the pilot we'll need your infra contacts for peering + an admin-level service account for KMS integration testing. We'll also export a minimal operator playbook.
[08:16] Carlos Reyes: I'll assign Evan to coordinate the peering.
[08:19] Evan Liu: Sounds good.
[08:21] Janelle Moore: One more technical: if we run a mixed fleet (some on-prem, some hosted), can you route specific user cohorts to on-prem models for extra privacy?
[08:30] Noah Rivera: Yep - routing policy supports attribute-based routing: you can set request metadata tags (e.g., tenant_id or cohort) and route those to a private pool. The Console lets you map attributes to pools.
[08:40] Maya Patel: Quick note — for mixed fleets we recommend harmonizing model artifacts and quantization profiles so fallbacks behave predictably.
[08:50] [09:00] -- Mid-call noise and brief audio glitch, transcription shows small garble --
[09:12] Liam Chen: I'm going to highlight a common pitfall: some customers pick a fastest int8 model but forget to run quality checks on long-form prompts; Optimize will usually show a delta there.
[09:24] Janelle Moore: We have long-form reporting use-cases — that matters.
[09:27] Liam Chen: Then include long sequences in the bench and run the int8 candidate through your evals. The catalog will mark if a model's long-form tokenization causes memory blowouts or kernel fallback.
[09:38] Carlos Reyes: Are there per-request encryption knobs? We need to ensure payloads are never logged in plaintext in any managed service.
[09:45] Noah Rivera: Redwoods hosted endpoints can be configured to not persist request/response bodies. For Private we recommend the default be 'never persist' and any logging to be forwarded encrypted to your buckets.
[09:56] Priya Iyer: Great. Could you put together a short runbook for the pilot that lists all required permissions and network steps?
[10:02] Maya Patel: Yes, action item for me to send that with the SOC2/KMS doc.
[10:07] Liam Chen: Back to the UI demo — I'm showing how to pin an artifact ID in the route config. If you pin, rollouts won't switch to newer builds unless you explicitly enable auto-upgrade. Useful for compliance.
[10:22] Janelle Moore: Good. We need explicit control.
[10:25] Maya Patel: We'll include that in the pilot runbook.
[10:28] [10:30] -- The rest of demo covers a quick bench run and interpreting a per-model prompt-level quality table --
[10:45] Liam Chen: See the prompt-level quality table - each row is a prompt group, columns show mean log-perplexity, BLEU-ish proxy, and a subjective flag for hallucination. You can drill into transcripts.
[10:59] Janelle Moore: That drilling looks helpful. Can we export the failed prompts?
[11:03] Liam Chen: Yes, export is built in, and you can attach notes for triage.
[11:08] Carlos Reyes: On the tag "requires custom kernel" - if a model needs an experimental kernel, what's the timeline to onboard it to our dedicated pool?
[11:15] Noah Rivera: If it's something we already support, it's quick — 1-3 days for validation. If it's experimental kernel dev, that might be a few weeks depending on kernel maturity and QA. We'll surface the risk in the artifact page.
[11:29] [11:30] -- Wrapping section --
[11:31] Maya Patel: Quick recap: we'll send SOC2/KMS doc + pilot runbook, Liam will attach bench exports and the Optimize short-guide, and we'll schedule the POC scoping call. Any blockers from Horizon side?
[11:42] Carlos Reyes: Procurement timeline TBD but no technical blockers. Priya will own infra sign-offs.
[11:47] Priya Iyer: Yup we'll follow up with Evan and schedule internal review.
[11:51] Maya Patel: Great. Last ask — Carlos, can you confirm the two intents you want in the sandbox by end of day tomorrow?
[11:58] Carlos Reyes: Yes we'll send the intents and a short trace.
[12:02] Maya Patel: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the sheet.
[12:06] Janelle Moore: Thanks, bye.
[12:08] Evan Liu: Bye.
[12:10] [12:12] End of recording. Notes: brief filler and some transcription mis-hearings around kernel names; see attached bench sheet link for detailed numbers.
